content: The FAM18B1 protein, also known as Family with sequence similarity 18 member B1, is a hypothetical protein encoded by the gene LOC51030. Evidence for the existence of this protein is currently limited to the transcript level, meaning it has been identified through its RNA but not yet confirmed at the protein level. This gene has two paralogs in the human genome: LOC201158, which is located on chromosome 17 at position 17p12, and TVP23A, which is located on chromosome 16. The duplication event that gave rise to these paralogs appears to have occurred after the most recent common ancestor (MRCA) of humans and apes. Additionally, this gene has homologs in eukaryotic organisms, with evolutionary conservation traceable as far back as Trichoplax, a simple multicellular organism. The gene LOC51030 is highly conserved among chordates and also shows conservation across a wide range of eukaryotes, including fungi and plants. It is located on chromosome 17, spanning the genomic region from 18,684,582 to 18,710,026 base pairs. The most common mRNA transcript of this gene contains seven exons and encodes a protein with a molecular weight of approximately 57 kDa. The protein contains a domain of unknown function, referred to as DUF846, and a predicted phosphoserine site, which may play a role in post-translational modifications. It is classified as a multipass transmembrane protein and is a member of the FAM18/TVP23 superfamily. FAM18B1 appears to be ubiquitously expressed across all tissues, health states, and developmental stages to varying degrees. Notably, there is significant expression of this gene in bladder tissue.
